clue.text: Be that excited (right of title-holder!) to get on with it?

definitions.text: Be that excited (right of title-holder!) to get on with it?

indicators.note: the anagram is placed to the right of, that is after, the title-holder

parts.note: a champ, short for champion, holds the title

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up, so the words be that and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An eager champion, revved up and impatient to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges BE THAT plus IT into ATTHEBIT, set to the right of CHAMP. The whole clue also describes the answer, so the definition and wordplay share words: a semi-&lit.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ at the bit is to be restlessly impatient to start, like a horse chewing its bit.

clue.text: Cross, rip off salad leaf

parts.note: chi is the Greek letter shaped like a cross, X
a con is a swindle, a rip-off

explanation.surface: Someone angry about being overcharged for lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicon is a name for a chicory head, the pale leaves eaten in salads.

clue.text: Perhaps porter has provided for big guy's penetrating film tune

indicators.note: the ale has, that is holds, the rest inside it

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ale

indicators.note: the run of short words penetrates the film's two letters, sitting between them

parts.note: GT is short for Gran Turismo, the 2023 motor-racing movie
if means provided, as in provided that
to can mean for, as in a present to someone
fat means big
his is a guy's

explanation.surface: A beer laid on for a large fellow who interrupts the movie music.
explanation.walkthrough: Gran Turismo is a 2023 movie, hence GT. 'A Gift of a Thistle' is a piece from James Horner's score for the movie Braveheart.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a named musical piece, an instrumental cue from the 1995 Braveheart soundtrack.

clue.text: Trashy book consumption on board P&O vessel

indicators.note: the disease goes on board, inside the ship's letters

parts.note: P and O, the shipping line, give the letters PO
an oiler is a ship carrying oil
consumption is an old name for tuberculosis, TB

explanation.surface: Someone reads cheap fiction and drinks on a cruise ship.
explanation.walkthrough: P&O is a British shipping and cruise company; 'on board' puts the disease inside its vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A potboiler is a hastily written novel produced purely to earn money.

clue.text: Sailor went smelling American plant

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
went, in the sense of went to the toilet, is wee'd

explanation.surface: A seaman goes off smelling of an American plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went' is the toilet sense: WEED is wee'd. 'smelling' links the pieces to the definition, since tarweed is notably fragrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarweed is a sticky, strong-scented plant of the daisy family native to the western US.

clue.text: Leaders of holy war brought down pilgrim

indicators.note: the leaders of a word are its first letters, here the opening pair
in a down entry, bringing letters down sends them to the bottom

parts.note: a jihad is a holy war

explanation.surface: Generals in a religious war shot down a traveller to Mecca.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders of' picks JI from JIHAD and 'brought down' moves them to the bottom, giving HAD + JI.
explanation.definitionFit: A hadji is a Muslim who has made the hajj, the pilgrimage to Mecca.

clue.text: Earl left college with stuck-up fellow wearing sibling's footwear

indicators.note: the sibling's letters wear the rest, wrapped round them

parts.note: brother's is a sibling's

indicators.note: in a down entry, the peer is pushed upward, so it is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a peer is a fellow, an equal

explanation.surface: An aristocrat quits university with a snooty friend, dressed in his brother's shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'stuck-up' turns the fellow upwards; 'wearing' means the sibling's letters are worn round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Brothel creepers are thick crepe-soled suede shoes associated with 1950s Teddy boys.

clue.text: What I do about keeping explosive Games news within range

indicators.note: the backward letters keep, or hold, the rest inside
about means turned round, so the setter's verb is read backwards

parts.note: the setter's job is to set puzzles
HE stands for high explosive
PE, physical education, is school games
news read as new plus new, N and N
in means within

explanation.surface: The setter describes keeping exciting sports news inside a mountain range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What I do' is the setter speaking: SET, turned 'about' to TES, holds HE, PE, NN and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pennines are a chain of hills running down northern England, the so-called backbone of the country.

clue.text: Took care of equine TV star in parts

indicators.note: the horse's name parts, opening up to let the word in sit inside it

parts.note: Mister Ed was the talking horse of a 1960s American sitcom

explanation.surface: Someone looks after a famous television horse in pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' splits MISTER ED after its M so that IN can go in.
explanation.definitionFit: To minister to someone is to attend to their needs, so ministered is a synonym of looked after.

clue.text: Like pie? Perhaps too much like eggs?

parts.note: over can mean excessive, as in over the top
the idiom easy as pie

explanation.surface: Musings on pie and on eggs, perhaps overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggs fried on both sides with a runny yolk are served over easy, a mainly American breakfast term.

clue.text: Didn't quite finish the meal just to your right

explanation.definitionFit: Leaving some food means not finishing a plate; as a direction it nudges slightly leftward, which for someone facing the speaker is a little to the right.

clue.text: Helium and nitrogen supply brief series of bangs!

indicators.note: supply read as the adverb meaning flexibly, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium

explanation.surface: Two gases are provided to fuel a short burst of explosions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' here is pronounced supp-lee, from supple, not the verb, so HE plus NITROGEN is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-nighter is a brief sexual fling, and bangs is slang for sexual encounters.

clue.text: Diss local plum pies during long drink of bubbly?

indicators.note: one anagram sits during, that is within, the span of the other
bubbly letters fizz about, so long drink of is rearranged
pie is printers' slang for jumbled type, so plum is mixed up

explanation.surface: Plum pies eaten while downing a long glass of champagne.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a market town in Norfolk, England. 'bubbly' rearranges the drink words, and the plum, jumbled by 'pies', goes 'during' that result.
explanation.definitionFit: Norfolk dumpling is an old nickname for a native of the county of Norfolk, where Diss lies.

clue.text: Elite competitors off cycling overwhelmed by millions of tits

parts.note: M is short for millions

indicators.note: cycling moves the opening letters round to the end

parts.note: an A-team is the top squad
off means ill, unwell

explanation.surface: Top athletes who feel sick on a bike ride are swamped by birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' sends the ATE of ATEAMILL to the back, giving AMILLATE, which sits under M. Tits here are not birds but nipples.
explanation.definitionFit: Mamillate means having nipples or nipple-like bumps, as tits is slang for breasts.

clue.text: Rotten MOD target setter called work

indicators.note: rotten letters fall apart and are rearranged

parts.note: the setter refers to himself as me
called on the phone, that is rung

explanation.surface: A bad Ministry of Defence target, and the setter phoned about the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rotten' rearranges MOD TARGET into GOTTERDAM. MOD is the UK Ministry of Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: Götterdämmerung is a Wagner opera, the last of his Ring cycle, so it is a musical work (opus).

clue.text: Perk up with, for instance, a Californian wine valley

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom

parts.note: eg means for instance
the Napa Valley in California is famous for wine

explanation.surface: Cheering up with a trip to a Californian wine region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns the whole run EG A NAPA, giving APANAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An apanage is a benefit or privilege attached to a position, a perquisite.

clue.text: Here on and off is alto, flourishing within limits of chancel

definitions.text: Here on and off is alto, flourishing within limits of chancel

indicators.note: the anagram goes inside the bounding letters of chancel
the limits of a word are its first and last letters
flourishing suggests a showy rearrangement of the letters
taking letters on and off picks the first and third of here

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An alto singer performs intermittently here, at the edge of the chancel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on and off' takes the first and third letters of Here; 'flourishing' mixes them with IS ALTO, and 'within' sets that between the first and last letters of chancel. The whole clue pictures where the singer sits.
explanation.definitionFit: A choir stall is a seat in the chancel of a church, where choristers such as altos sing during services.

clue.text: Aptly heads embarking on special boat

indicators.note: the toilets embark on, getting inside, the special letters

parts.note: the heads are a ship's toilets, so a loo

explanation.surface: Fitting that the leaders board a dedicated vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aptly' notes that heads, the naval word for toilets, suits a boat clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a single-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: See 9
See 10
Obsessive captain following order on every landing site

indicators.note: the captain follows the order

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit
Captain Ahab, monomaniac hunter of the whale in Moby-Dick
each means every

explanation.surface: A fixated sea captain obeys orders about every landing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts the captain after the order; 'on' just links the last piece. Ahab is the whale-obsessed captain of Moby-Dick.
explanation.definitionFit: Omaha Beach was one of the D-Day landing beaches in Normandy in 1944.

clue.text: See 1 down
Extrovert outcasts do work on cases

indicators.note: the do-work-on letters encase the outcasts

parts.note: to ape is to imitate, to do an impression
op is short for opus, a work
lepers were historically shunned outcasts

explanation.surface: Social rejects take on legal cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases' means the three short pieces are wrapped around the outcasts, split after their first five letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is outgoing and enjoys others' company is called a people person.
